title: Pinned model continuity orchestration and failover policy
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Teams pin model versions for deterministic behavior (compatibility, QA, compliance). When the pinned variant becomes unavailable (regional outage, resource exhaustion, or deprecation) we presently rely on ad-hoc hand-offs or coarse fallback rules which cause either high-latency spillovers or silent quality regressions.

Goal: Define and implement a deterministic orchestration and policy layer that preserves continuity for pinned model routes while minimizing latency and quality regression. This ticket scopes the policy model, control-plane contract, runtime enforcement hooks, observability requirements, and the operator playbook for deprecation-driven transitions.

Non-goals: Model training/rollout tooling, license negotiations, and billing model changes are out of scope for this ticket.
acceptance_criteria: Policy engine can express a per-pin ordered priority matrix: (region, variant, quantized_variant, fallback_model) with explicit reason and TTL
Runtime honors per-request policy and records decision trace (route_reason, chosen_variant, fallback_origin) for every pinned route
Automatic deprecation progression: soft-warning -> reduced-weight -> enforced-fallback with configurable grace windows per pin
No customer traffic is routed to an incompatible variant without automatic compatibility checks and explicit override
Telemetry dashboards surface pin continuity SLI (pinned_success_rate, avg_fallback_latency, quality_regression_incidents) and alerting rules are defined
proposed_solution_summary: Introduce a 'continuity policy' resource attached to pinned versions. The policy is a small declarative object (JSON/YAML) that lists prioritized targets (region + variant), compatibility constraints (max_context_len, kv_cache_compatible: true|false), deprecation windows, and a health-weighting function. The control plane exposes APIs to publish policies during onboarding and to mutate them (canary increases, emergency cutovers). The serving runtime gets a compact decision function and emits a trace event so Console and Optimize can evaluate cost/quality trade-offs in real time.
config_example:
continuity_policy:
  pinned_version: model-v4.3.1
  priorities:
    - region: us-west-2
      variant: v4.3.1-gpu
      kv_cache_compatible: true
      max_context: 8192
      reason: primary
    - region: us-east-1
      variant: v4.3.1-cpu-quant
      kv_cache_compatible: false
      max_context: 4096
      reason: 'regional-fallback'
  deprecation: 
    soft_warning_days: 14
    reduced_weight_days: 7
    enforced_after_days: 21
  compatibility_checks:
    - kv_cache_compatibility
    - tokenizer_hash_match
  ttl_seconds: 3600
detailed_tasks: Design: policy schema + API contract (control-plane) and decision contract (runtime)
Implementation: control-plane storage, UI editor in Console, and publishing API for onboarding flow
Runtime: fast decision path that evaluates priority list with health signals and compatibility checks
Observability: traces, per-pin metrics, synthetic canary traffic generator, and Console dashboards
Operator playbook: deprecation escalation steps, emergency override, and rollback steps
E2E tests: simulated regional outage, variant incompatibility, KV cache mismatch tests, and golden-quality check against baseline prompts
progress_updates: 2025-09-03 — Aisha: Drafted initial problem statement and sketched policy schema. Linked to onboarding PRD.
2025-09-08 — Marco: Implemented prototype policy parser in the dev branch (refs: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/782). Initial unit tests added.

2025-09-12 — SRE (Liam): Ran regional outage sim and confirmed runtime decision path can be exercised with synthetic traffic. Observed increased latency for cross-region fallback; added metric 'fallback_cross_region_p50'.
2025-09-18 — Product (Evelyn): Reviewed policy UX flows in Console. Requested a clear 'deprecation countdown' visible in onboarding flow and an audit log entry for all automatic transitions.
2025-09-22 — Marco: Added compatibility checks (tokenizer hash + kv cache capability). Leaving a flag for canary behavioral rollout. Runtime PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/841
2025-09-25 — Aisha: Draft operator playbook and alert thresholds. Need sign-off from Security for KMS usage when policy includes variant-specific encryption keys.
decision_log: 2025-09-10: Consensus to make compatibility checks mandatory in policy (no silent fallthrough to incompatible variants).
2025-09-14: Agreed deprecation default windows: 14d soft warning, 7d reduced weight, 21d enforced. Allow per-pin overrides for enterprise customers.
2025-09-20: Chose to surface decision traces at token-level for 1% sampled traffic and aggregated per-route for all traffic to avoid excessive telemetry cost.
open_questions: How should billing reflect cross-region failovers for Dedicated customers? (Finance input required)
Should we allow a 'best-effort-compat' option where non-critical routes can accept minor tokenizer differences with explicit opt-in?
What SLA language is appropriate when an enforced-fallback occurs due to customer-configured deprecation?
acceptance_test_plan: Create a pinned route with primary in us-west-2 and secondary in eu-west-1; kill primary, validate traffic moves to secondary within 2s for 90th percentile, and record decision traces.
Publish a pin with kv_cache_compatible: true on primary and false on fallback; send requests that rely on KV cache and verify fallback is rejected and logged (no silent downgrade).
Trigger a deprecation window and assert Console shows countdown, reduced-weight phase reduces traffic to target percentage, and enforced phase triggers automatic rerouting.
notes_and_followups: Follow up with Security to review KMS key rotation when variant-specific keys are referenced in policies (assigned to Priya, due 2025-09-30).
Coordinate with Console team for a UX stub by 2025-09-29 to show deprecation countdown and audit history (EPIC: CON-1423).
Add a migration helper to transform existing naive fallthrough rules into continuity_policy with conservative defaults.
